name: artifact-based build-deploy-observe
summary: Remote servers become deployment and acceptance targets. Source changes originate in the development workspace; an installed wheel carrying its own build identity is what reaches a host. L2 and above now require an installed artifact traceable to a committed source state.

iterations.observation: wheel built without kultrun/BUILD.json: it is gitignored so a stale build identity can never be committed, and hatchling honours VCS ignore files. Every deployed instance would have reported itself as a source checkout.
iterations.correction: explicit hatchling artifacts force-include, pinned by test_the_build_identity_is_force_included_in_the_wheel
iterations.outcome: manifest ships in the wheel; source tree still left clean

iterations.observation: clean install and host discovery both correct; fingerprint identical to accepted Stage 1.1. Three cosmetic/observability defects and one real product gap found: empty artifact field, 2.15 PB printed as '2002393.6 GiB', /v1/version untested, and no way to configure a deployed instance.
iterations.correction: dropped the unknowable field, scaled byte output, added the version route test; recorded K-20 and K-21 rather than fixing product configuration in a workflow task

iterations.observation: upgrade over the existing deployment; hwloc and prior state preserved, same host_id and fingerprint, mount now reads 1.9 PiB

END_LINK.next: Stage 1.2 — capacity, using build -> deploy -> observe -> fix

modes.upgrade: most iterations; preserves provisioned components, models, caches, configuration and evidence
modes.clean_install: periodic and at milestone gates; next required at the Milestone 1 L4 gate, or earlier if installation or provisioning behaviour materially changes

stage_1_1.note: last stage accepted from a source tree; retrospective note added to its stage package, acceptance untouched
